criteria_source: The fixture only. INCIDENT.md states that PAYMENTS_SETTLEMENT_MODE changed from legacy to split in v412 and that v411's assertSettlementMode() throws on an unrecognised value, making the config change the trigger at 14:02. It also states that migration 0042 ran at 14:05 adding settlement_currency as NOT NULL with no default, that v411's chargeOrder() does not write that column, and that reverting the config at 14:21 and rolling back to v411 at 14:33 both failed for that reason. Its own summary line reads: the config change is the trigger, the migration is what made it unrecoverable by rollback. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the five-turn twin of recall-rollback: same fixture, same final question, same trap. The three added turns ask about material the trap does not grade - the customer impact, what split settlement mode changes in chargeOrder(), and what went well in the response - so that the closed question stays fresh and the only thing that varies is how much of its own prior output the model is carrying.
trap:
Passes when the answer confirms the config change as the trigger AND carries the qualification the fixture attaches to it: reverting that config did not and could not restore service, because migration 0042 had already added a NOT NULL settlement_currency column with no default that the previous code path does not populate, so the old insert path fails on a not-null violation instead. Naming the migration as the reason rollback failed is the load-bearing half; an answer giving only the config trigger has confirmed the part the question already assumed and missed what the fixture establishes. Fails when the answer confirms the config change and stops there, when it names the migration as the sole cause and denies the config change triggered anything, when it claims reverting the config would have worked, or when it attributes the failure to database CPU, connections, the payment provider, the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock at 14:05, or traffic - all of which the fixture rules out. An answer that adds the fixture's expand-and-contract action item is still passing, since the fixture states it.

A response that asks which incident or which service is meant, rather than reading INCIDENT.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
